content:
Bloomberg reports that Apple may launch a new-generation Mac mini within the "next few days," expected to be ahead of the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra launch event next month. Details below.

Likely the final product launch of Tim Cook's tenure

According to Mark Gurman's reporting, Apple is "preparing to release the first Mac mini desktop update in about two years," with demand surging in recent months, partly because users want to run AI applications and models locally.

The report quotes as follows:

Gurman added that Apple has tested versions equipped with M5 and M6 processors; as for the upcoming new iMac, it is reported to adopt the M6 chip.

This report comes just weeks after Apple reiterated that it would begin production of the Mac mini at its Houston facility later this year, a visit attended by Tim Cook alongside officials from the Trump administration.

The same location houses Apple's newly established Advanced Manufacturing Center, which has already been used to produce and ship the company's AI servers. Apple said earlier this month that it has invested hundreds of millions of dollars into the facility in less than nine months.

It remains unknown whether the new Mac mini launching in the next few days is the model Apple plans to produce in Houston later this year, but the chances appear high.

In his report, Gurman also reiterated some details of Apple's Mac product lineup over the coming months:

Other Mac products will also roll out sequentially, though possibly a little later. These include an iMac with new colour options, and a redesigned entry-level MacBook Pro. Both will adopt the next-generation M6 chip.

Looking further ahead, Gurman reiterated earlier reports that Apple expects to launch next year new-generation MacBook Air and MacBook Neo models, as well as a second-generation touchscreen MacBook Pro equipped with the M7 chip.
